target_customer: Runners, cyclists and triathletes who book races, and event organizers who pay fees and use the registration platform
problem: Finding and signing up for endurance events meant scattered organizer sites and fragmented registration tools. Let's Do This built one marketplace with personalized recommendations and later a registration platform for organizers.
business_model: Marketplace and registration platform with a take or fee on event registrations, plus data and listing partnerships
product_category: Endurance events marketplace and registration software

founders.name: Sam Browne
education: Cambridge (per NBC and alumni pieces, met Rose at Cambridge)
founders.background_notes: Described by TechCrunch 2022 as an endurance runner and cyclist, childhood friend of Rose.

founders.name: Alex Rose
education: Cambridge (per NBC, met Browne at Cambridge)
founders.background_notes: Endurance runner and cyclist per TechCrunch 2022.

competitors.name: RunSignup
competitors.what: Race registration and technology platform for race directors in the US
competitors.traction_then: Estimated 20 to 30 percent US registration market share per its own 2018 analysis (self reported)

technical_complexity.rationale: A listings marketplace with search, personalization and later a registration system. The hard parts were data aggregation and organizer integrations, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided marketplace with a large catalogue (about 30,000 races in 2019) and exclusive publisher partnerships such as Hearst, but registration platforms like RunSignup and others were established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it directly; it expanded into registration software and signed organizer partnerships through 2026.

market_need_then: Mass participation races were growing and registration was fragmented; the company cites an estimated 18 billion dollar global endurance market and reported over 5 million users by June 2022.

branding.domain_note: letsdothis.com in use; acquisition detail not found

identity.logo: October 2021 rebrand removed the underscore and added a route motif
identity.visual_style: Volt Yellow palette, bold lettering drawn from handwritten spectator signs, Bossa and Pilat typefaces
identity.voice_and_tone: Voice of the people, celebratory and encouraging; brand idea Moments Make Us

branding.brand_signature: Handwritten spectator sign style and Volt Yellow

rebrands.to: Nomad designed identity, Moments Make Us
rebrands.why: Brand lacked personality and cohesion per the VP of product design; post lockdown focus on accessible events

branding.community_and_virality: Celebrity backers (Serena Williams, Usain Bolt, Paula Radcliffe) and a No Excuses T-shirt seen in press photos; no organized fan community found in opened sources.

brand_strength.rationale: Celebrity investors and a strong 2021 identity helped awareness, and the company reported over 5 million users, but no evidence it was a primary growth driver.

pivots.why: Company partnership releases through 2025 and 2026 describe an AI Registration Platform for organizers; exact date not sourced

outcome_analysis: Let's Do This raised a 5 million seed and 15 million Series A in 2019 and a 60 million Series B in 2022 on a catalogue of about 30,000 races, publisher partnerships and celebrity backing. It has since moved toward selling registration software to organizers, with a five year London Marathon Events deal announced in January 2025. A founder comment quoted in an alumni piece suggests revenue held while headcount fell, but no layoff report was opened, so the later trajectory is only partly documented.
notes: Company website returned 403 and was not worked around. YC says founded 2017, TechCrunch 2022 says 2016, press says set up July 2017. The Series A and seed both occurred in late 2019, after the Winter 2018 batch. Total raised conflicts across outlets (NBC about 31M, TechRound 21.4M); no round is recorded from totals. RunSignup is the only dated competitor found; its share figure is self reported and the source is a March 2018 market analysis page whose text was not opened (only the search summary). Outcome search found partnerships, no acquisition or shutdown.
